examples.text: Municipal Guard in al-Kuwaifiya (West of #Benghazi) dispose of 13,000 frozen chickens unfit for consumption. #Libya…
examples.diagnosis: Written as a factual news report with no opinion words; the negativity is in the event itself (food unfit for consumption), so the model reads the reporting tone as neutral.

examples.text: @user In other related news\u002c you know there\u2019s no Parks tomorrow?
examples.diagnosis: The complaint is implied (disappointment that the show is not on) and phrased as a plain question; with no negative words on the surface the model defaults to neutral.

examples.text: With James Comey in office, how could the US investigate the Russians? @user @user @user  @user
examples.diagnosis: A rhetorical question that criticises by implication; understanding it as negative needs political context, and there is no explicit negative wording to pick up.

examples.text: @user I still think it was fake. I always thought Nicki to be the type to call you out on a random Tuesday, not at an awards show"
examples.diagnosis: A hedged, conversational opinion where the only negative cue is the word "fake"; the long neutral explanation after it outweighs that cue.

examples.text: @user It seems even Nobel prize is for sale. Amartya Sen then and Bob Dylan  now
examples.diagnosis: Sarcasm: the criticism is carried by the "for sale" jab at the Nobel prize, not by negative vocabulary, so the literal wording looks neutral.
